why: reported score 0.666667 for a flat array; matches triangle computation.
statement: Constant heights (a single box) give R=2/3 because f*f is triangular.

For symmetric f the peak of f*f is ||f||_2^2, hence R=||f*f||_2^2/(||f||_1^2||f||_2^2)=(∫u^2)/(∫u) with u=(f*f)/max; so R is large exactly when f*f is flat/rectangle-like. A box gives a triangular f*f (R=2/3); a smooth bump gives a flatter-topped f*f, so it should exceed 2/3.
refuted_if: a symmetric f whose measured R disagrees with this formula, or a smooth bump scoring below a box.

statement: Among compactly supported f the supremum of R is strictly above 2/3 and at least near 1/√2≈0.7071 (Gaussian); likely attained by a smooth single bump, not a rectangle.
refuted_if: a broad search showing every single bump stays at or below 2/3, or a construction far above 1/√2.

why: Both top programs have asymmetric f*f peaks (max at 0.324 and 0.562 of support) and score 0.80+.
statement: For symmetric f the peak of f*f is ||f||_2^2 and R=(∫u^2)/(∫u) with u=(f*f)/max, so R is large when f*f is flat/rectangle-like; but an ASYMMETRIC f has max(f*f)<||f||_2^2 (Cauchy-Schwarz equality needs symmetry), lowering the denominator and raising R when the bulk of f*f is preserved.

The supremum of R is at least 0.8078, attained by an asymmetric, flat-topped single bump, and lies well above 1/sqrt(2)≈0.7071; the rectangle limit R→1 is unreachable because f*f of nonneg f is continuous and vanishes at the support edges.
refuted_if: a broad search showing all asymmetric flat-top bumps saturate below 0.808, or a construction far above 0.81.

why: p0004 0.8078 and p0006 0.8034 both come from height optimization, vs 0.7437 for the best parametric family.
statement: Direct height-vector optimization from smooth or flat-top seeds reaches R≥0.80, far above any fixed parametric family (best family 0.7437).

why: p0005's flat-top exp-power (p>2) reached 0.7437 > 0.7071.
statement: Flat-topped f produce flat-topped, more rectangle-like f*f, raising R above the Gaussian's 0.7071.
refuted_if: a flat-top profile family that never beats the Gaussian across its parameters.

why: p0012 raises the best lower bound to 0.833835, and p0011 shows a second high-scoring shape class.
statement: The supremum of R is at least 0.833835, reached by p0012's asymmetric tilted shape; p0011's near-symmetric multi-scale shape reaches 0.829953, so high R is not unique to one asymmetric profile. The rectangle limit remains unreachable because f*f of nonnegative f is continuous and vanishes at support edges.

why: p0012 is strongly asymmetric with low peak, but p0011 is near-symmetric and still reaches 0.8300, so asymmetry helps but may not be strictly necessary.
statement: For symmetric f the peak of f*f is ||f||_2^2 and R=(int u^2)/(int u) with u=(f*f)/max, so R is large when f*f is flat/rectangle-like; an asymmetric f generally has max(f*f)<||f||_2^2, lowering the denominator and raising R when the bulk of f*f is preserved. However, high R may also be reachable near-symmetrically if f*f is flat enough.

why: These are the two strongest results so far and suggest both asymmetry and resolution/refinement matter.
statement: A monotone exponential tilt h*exp(lambda*(2x-1)) with lambda around 1, followed by block reoptimization, gives a large gain on the p0004 line (0.807751 to 0.833835); multi-scale refinement from a symmetric seed also reaches 0.829953.

why: p0019's symmetric-constrained optimization kept the full 0.833835, refuting the claim that asymmetry is what lowers ||f*f||inf.
statement: R is large when f*f is flat and rectangle-like with a suppressed peak. A symmetric f can achieve this as well as an asymmetric one (symmetrizing p0012 retained R=0.833835), so asymmetry is NOT required — the lever is peak suppression / flatness of f*f, not f's asymmetry.

why: New best 0.837273 and evidence that symmetry is not limiting.
statement: The supremum of R is at least 0.837273 (p0018); high R is reachable by both asymmetric (p0016/p0018) and symmetric (p0019) profiles, and the gap to 1 comes from the unavoidable tails of f*f for nonnegative f.

why: Both deepen slots gained independently from the same start.
statement: Two complementary mechanisms each raise R by ~0.003 over p0012: targeted dip suppression at the f*f peak (p0016: 0.836911) and mass-preserving multi-scale resampling with block-ascent restarts (p0018: 0.837273).

why: p0019 retained the full score under symmetry, suggesting the symmetric subspace is not limiting.
statement: Because R depends only on f*f, a symmetric-constrained search (half the degrees of freedom) can reach the same optimum with finer effective resolution; symmetry is a useful search-space reduction, not a restriction on achievable R.
refuted_if: a symmetric-constrained optimizer that consistently scores well below the free asymmetric optimum.
a broad search showing all flat-top/nonnegative bumps saturate well below 0.8386, or a construction far above 0.84.

text: R is maximized by nonnegative f whose convolution is as flat and rectangle-like as possible, with a suppressed f*f peak; symmetry is not required. Direct height-vector optimization from smooth/flat-top seeds, exponential tilts, targeted dip suppression, and multi-scale block-ascent restarts are the productive mechanisms. The current best is 0.838635 (p0025), from combining dip suppression with multi-scale restarts. Parametric flat-top families are much weaker, and proper gradients add little. The remaining gap to 1 likely comes from tails/peak constraints; compact-support and symmetric searches are the main open tests.

why: Every combination of these mechanisms on the p0012/p0018 line produced a real gain.
statement: Targeted dip suppression at the f*f peak, mass-preserving multi-scale resampling with block-ascent restarts, and (per the mutation loop) progressive upsampling to N=6000-13000 are complementary and compose: p0016 0.836911, p0018 0.837273, p0025 0.838635, p0022 0.838395, p0024 0.838491.

why: Lower bound moved up again; tail-limit claim still unverified.
statement: The best known R is 0.838635 (p0025); high R is reachable by both asymmetric and symmetric profiles, and the gap to 1 is plausibly due to the unavoidable tails/structure of f*f for nonnegative f, but this is untested against compact-support constructions.

why: Both mutation-loop records and p0025's own restart stage show gains concentrated at higher N and stronger dip scans.
statement: Refining at progressively higher resolution (N from ~1000 up to 6000-13000) with block ascent at each level yields real gains (~+0.001) beyond the N=1000 optimum, because finer steps resolve the flat top of f*f; reallocating budget away from weak tilt/warmup stages into stronger dip scans also pays.
refuted_if: Two independent high-resolution runs starting from p0025 fail to beat its N=1000 score by any real margin.

why: p0023 gained much less than dip-based p0016/p0024 from the same start.
statement: Random smooth additive bump perturbations of the height vector (p0023) add only ~0.0006, well below targeted multiplicative dips; they are not a strong structural lever.

why: Lower bound moved to 0.839812; compact-support test p0030 supports the tail view.
statement: The best known R is now 0.839812 (p0026). High R is reachable by both asymmetric and symmetric profiles; compact-support scratch shapes (p0030, 0.801040) are much weaker, consistent with the gap to 1 being a tail/structure effect of nonnegative f*f.

why: Every fused variant gained; p0026/p0027 are the current records.
statement: Targeted dip suppression, mass-preserving multi-scale resampling with block-ascent restarts, progressive upsampling, and (mutation loop) an early fine polish plus restarts that grow N to 4000 are complementary and compose: p0025 0.838635, p0029 0.839329, p0031 0.838921, p0026 0.839812, p0027 0.839798.

why: p0029 gained at N=4000→8000; p0026 grew N to 4000 for its gain.
statement: Refining at progressively higher resolution (N up to 8000-13000) with block ascent at each level yields real gains beyond the N=1000-2000 optimum; p0029 confirms N=4000→8000 with fine blocks adds +0.0007.

why: p0029 exceeded its 0.8388 threshold using exactly this.
statement: Fine block sizes (2-6) with decaying steps plus narrow Gaussian dips (widths 0.01-0.06) at N=4000-8000 give a real gain (+0.0007, p0029 0.839329) and are distinct from coarse dips.

why: Both mutation-loop variants are the current records.
statement: An early short fine local polish, a tightened dip scan, and restarts that grow N toward 4000 give a big gain on p0025 (p0026 0.839812, p0027 0.839798).

The best known R is now 0.840232 (p0037). High R is reachable by asymmetric and symmetric profiles; compact-support scratch shapes (p0030, 0.801040) are much weaker, consistent with the gap to 1 being a tail/structure effect of nonnegative f*f.
refuted_if: A broad search showing all flat-top/nonnegative bumps saturate well below 0.8402, or a construction far above 0.84.

why: p0037 and p0034 are the strongest results and use these mechanisms.
statement: Targeted dip suppression, mass-preserving multi-scale resampling with block-ascent restarts, progressive upsampling to N=20000 with per-level block refinement, and fine-block/narrow-dip high-N polishing are complementary and compose: p0037 0.840232, p0034 0.840208, p0025 0.838635.

Refining at progressively higher resolution (N up to 20000) with block ascent at each level yields real gains beyond N=1000-2000, but the last N=13000->20000 step of p0037 was only +0.000011, so high-N gains are near saturation.
refuted_if: Independent high-resolution runs from p0037 fail to beat 0.840232 by more than 0.00005, or a much higher N gives a large gain.

why: p0034 confirms the fine-dip line at higher resolution.
statement: Fine block sizes (2-6) with decaying steps plus narrow Gaussian dips (widths 0.005-0.06) at N=4000-13000 give real gains: p0029 +0.0007 and p0034 +0.0004 to 0.840208.

A symmetric-constrained search with the full p0026 recipe matched the free p0026 optimum exactly (p0035 0.839812), so symmetry is a useful search-space reduction, not a restriction at that resolution; it has not yet been pushed to N=20000.
refuted_if: A symmetric high-N search consistently scores more than 0.0005 below the free optimum.

why: p0038 improved the record and p0041 confirmed deconvolution is weak; compact support remains weak.
statement: The best known R is now 0.840911 (p0038). High R is reachable by asymmetric and symmetric profiles; compact-support scratch shapes and flat-target deconvolution are much weaker (0.79-0.80), consistent with the gap to 1 being a tail/structure effect of nonnegative f*f.
refuted_if: A construction far above 0.84, or a compact-support/deconvolution shape reaching above 0.84.

why: All three recent high-N variants gained on their starts.
statement: Targeted dip suppression, mass-preserving progressive upsampling to N=20000-30000 with per-level block refinement, fine-block (2-6) polishing, and restarts are complementary and compose: p0038 0.840911, p0043 0.840536, p0040 0.840441.

why: The previous near-saturation conjecture was contradicted by p0038 and p0043.
statement: High-resolution gains continue beyond N=13000: p0038 gained +0.00068 at N=20000 and p0043 gained +0.000305 by resampling to N=30000. High-N refinement is not yet saturated.
refuted_if: Independent high-N runs fail to beat 0.840911 by more than 0.0001, or a test of N=40000-50000 gives no real gain.

why: Both fine-block and narrow-dip mechanisms gained again at high N.
statement: Fine block sizes (2-6) with decaying steps plus narrow Gaussian dips (widths 0.002-0.06) at N=4000-30000 give real gains: p0029 +0.0007, p0034 +0.0004, p0040 +0.0002, p0043 +0.0003.

why: The flat-top mechanism is subsumed by B2's peak-suppression/flatness belief and no longer guides experiments.
p0041 was the dedicated deconvolution explore and was much weaker.
statement: Target-driven deconvolution of a flat-top f*f target (p0041) scores only 0.791, far below direct height optimization; it is not a competitive construction region.

why: Both new children of p0038 gained, confirming the recipe composes, though gains are now only 5-8e-5.
statement: Targeted dip suppression, mass-preserving progressive upsampling to N=20000-40000 with per-level block refinement, fine-block (2-6) polishing, and restarts are complementary and compose: p0038 0.840911, p0043 0.840536, p0045 0.840995, p0049 0.840961.

why: N=30000-40000 still pays, but only ~5-8e-5 per step, so the marginal value of N is falling.
statement: High-resolution gains continue beyond N=13000 but shrink with N: p0038 +0.00068 at N=20000, p0043 +0.000305 to N=30000, p0045 +0.000084 to N=40000, p0049 +0.000050 to N=30000. High-N is not yet saturated but is close.

why: p0049 confirms the narrow-dip lever at N=30000, but the gain is now small.
statement: Fine block sizes (2-6) with decaying steps plus narrow Gaussian dips (widths 0.002-0.06) at N=4000-40000 give real gains: p0029 +0.0007, p0034 +0.0004, p0040 +0.0002, p0043 +0.0003, p0049 +0.00005.

why: Best advanced only marginally to 0.840995; the conjecture is unchanged in substance.
statement: The best known R is now 0.840995 (p0045). High R is reachable by asymmetric and symmetric profiles; compact-support scratch shapes and flat-target deconvolution are much weaker (0.79-0.80), consistent with the gap to 1 being a tail/structure effect of nonnegative f.

why: Superseded by B7/B11; the p0026-recipe details are no longer the active lever.
Full-convolution scoring is O(N^2) per block trial, so only a few coarse moves fit per stage; the delta update is O(N·b), ~1000x cheaper, enabling much finer descent.
statement: Exact incremental O(N·b) delta-convolution score updates make block-1/2 coordinate descent at N=20000-40000 affordable and will yield gains of at least 0.0001 beyond full-convolution block ascent.
refuted_if: An incremental-score block-1/2 optimizer at N=20000-40000 gains less than 0.00005 over p0045 (0.840995).
A construction far above 0.841, or a compact-support/deconvolution shape reaching above 0.841.
A high-N run (N≥60000) with a genuinely different optimizer gains ≥0.0001 over 0.840999.

text: Current best is 0.840999 (p0052). R is maximized by nonnegative f whose convolution is flat and rectangle-like with a suppressed peak; symmetry is not required. Direct height optimization, exponential tilts, targeted dips, multi-scale block ascent, and progressive upsampling are productive. High-N resampling and exact incremental delta scoring are now saturated near 0.8410. The p0037 alternate basin is lower (0.840844). Target deconvolution and compact-support scratch shapes are weak. Next tests: escape the plateau via randomized basin hopping, test high-N mirror symmetry, and try a multi-lobe construction from scratch.

why: Three independent escape attempts each moved the score by <1e-5.
statement: Best known R is 0.840999 (p0052). A hard plateau at ~0.8410 now holds across N=20000-80000 and across full-convolution, exact incremental, dip, fine-block and basin-hop optimizers; the gap to 1 is a structural (non-negativity + autoconvolution) effect, not a resolution effect.

why: The predicted >=0.0001 gain did not materialize; the trend p0038 +0.00068 -> p0045 +0.000084 -> p0053 +0.000002 is monotonically decaying.
statement: High-N is saturated: resampling p0045 to N=60000 and N=80000 with the fast incremental block-1/2 optimizer gains only +0.000002 (p0053). N=40000 is the practical resolution ceiling; extra N buys nothing.

why: Predicted >=0.0001 gain; measured +0.000004.
statement: Exact incremental O(N*b) delta-convolution scoring makes block-1/2 descent affordable at N=40000 but yields only +0.000004 over p0045's coarse-block ascent (p0054): the full-convolution scorer was NOT the bottleneck, so the plateau is a property of the shape, not of the optimizer's cost.

why: The C-S argument plus the measured off-center peak positions explain why the symmetric line stalled at 0.8398.
statement: Mirror symmetry about 0.5 matched the free optimum at low resolution (p0035) but is a genuine restriction at high resolution: for f symmetric about 0.5, f*f attains its max at the center (Cauchy-Schwarz), whereas both best high-N solutions have the f*f max at 0.54-0.57 of support. Symmetry about a shifted center c is the natural reduced parametrization.

why: Superseded: the basin-hopping test subsumes the question of whether large non-local perturbations help, and small additive bumps are known weak.
Explains the off-center f*f peak seen in every high-scoring solution and gives a concrete reduced parametrization to test.
statement: f*f is always symmetric about the center of f's support. If f is symmetric about 0.5 then f*f's maximum is at the center; the best solutions instead peak at 0.54-0.57 of support, consistent with f being approximately symmetric about a shifted center c~0.55-0.57 (support roughly [2c-1,1]). This is why mirror symmetry about 0.5 is limiting and shifted symmetry about a free c is the right reduced parametrization.
refuted_if: A free-optimized f whose f*f max is at the center scoring >=0.8410, or a shifted-symmetry-constrained run scoring >=0.0005 below the free optimum.

why: p0057 beats the plateau by +0.00028; the plateau is recipe-specific.
statement: The ~0.8410 'plateau' is a property of the high-N local-ascent recipe, not of the problem: a low-N (N=1250) shape with dip suppression, gradient polish and many noisy block restarts reached 0.841275 (p0057), while high-N fine-block ascent, exact incremental scoring and basin hopping all stalled at ~0.8410 (p0052, p0054, p0060).

why: Incremental scoring gave no real gain (p0054) and is superseded by the low-N restart finding; low value.
p0061's shifted-symmetry-constrained run scored ~0.001 below the free best, and p0057's f*f peaks at 0.719, outside the claimed c~0.55-0.57 range; the conjecture is not supported.
Restarts at low N explore basins cheaply; high-N ascent gets stuck in one.
statement: Low-N (N~1000-2500) height vectors optimized with dip suppression + gradient polish + many noisy block restarts outperform high-N (40000) fine-block ascent: p0057 0.841275 vs p0052 0.840999, and the gain came almost entirely from the restart stage (0.840474 -> 0.841275).

why: p0066 at 0.842618 is far above 0.841 and comes from a different recipe (tiny-N global search), confirming the plateau was recipe-specific and showing the tiny-N search is the bigger lever.
statement: The ~0.8410 'plateau' was a property of the high-N local-ascent recipe, not of the problem. Two escapes now exist: the low-N noisy-restart recipe on the p0057 line reaches 0.841520 (p0067), and a tiny-N (N=200) global random-restart search upscaled to N=1250 reaches 0.842618 (p0066), the latter being the strongest lever found so far.

why: p0066 is the current record and beats every local-ascent and restart-line result.
statement: A tiny-N (N~200) global random-restart search (150 random log-normal / Gaussian-bump inits, block ascent, keep top few) upscaled 200->500->1250 with noisy restarts reaches 0.842618 (p0066), a new best and +0.0011 over the p0057 restart line.

why: p0066's flatness metrics differ sharply from the lower-scoring p0067/p0065 and it scores highest.
statement: The p0066 basin scores high with a much flatter f (max/mean 2.59) and a flatter f*f peak (7.56% of knots within 0.1% of max) than the p0057 line (max/mean 4.08, 1.12%), with the f*f max at 0.443 (left of center); this suggests a broad flat f*f top, not a sharp peak, is what raises R.
refuted_if: A shape with a sharp f*f peak (few knots near max) scoring above 0.8426.

why: Old exponential-tilt mechanism from the p0004 line; not driving current work.
Deconvolution is clearly noncompetitive and settled; free the slot.
p0070 symmetric forced search scored 0.715, far below the free 0.8426 — symmetry is a genuine restriction.
statement: Mirror symmetry about the center is a severe restriction at high resolution: forcing symmetry drives f*f's max to the center (Cauchy-Schwarz) and collapses the score (p0070: symmetrized p0066 fell to 0.715 vs 0.8426 free).

why: p0072 has only 2.00% of f*f knots within 0.1% of max (a sharp peak) yet scores 0.8524, far above p0066's flat-peak 0.8426 — the 'flat 0.1% peak' claim is refuted.
p0072's bigger seeded tiny-N search jumped +0.0098, confirming and strengthening the tiny-N lever.
statement: A tiny-N global random-restart search (N0~200-250) with block ascent and mass-preserving upscale is the strongest lever: 150 inits gave 0.842618 (p0066), and 250 inits seeded with the current best + top-10 upscale gave 0.852421 (p0072) — a richer basin landscape than local ascent.

why: p0072 is the largest single gain in many generations and came entirely from the scaled tiny-N search.
statement: Scaling the tiny-N (N0=250) global search (250 seeded inits, top-10 upscale 250->500->1250, long restart loop) found a new basin at 0.852421, +0.0098 over p0066; the basin search is far from saturated and its upscale+restart stages contributed +0.0054 and +0.0046.

why: p0069 gained on the p0066 basin with the restart+N-growth recipe.
statement: Low-N (N~1000-2500) height vectors with noisy block restarts + N growth keep paying: p0069 added +0.000588 to p0066 (0.843206), confirming the restart recipe is not saturated on a good basin.

why: p0072 broke through every prior plateau by a wide margin.
statement: Successive 'plateaus' (0.8410, 0.8426, 0.8432) were all recipe-specific artifacts, not problem limits: the tiny-N global search has now reached 0.852421 (p0072), so no plateau so far has been a true ceiling.

why: p0076 is a big gain from scaling the same recipe.
statement: Scaling the tiny-N global search keeps paying: N0=250/250 inits gave 0.852421 (p0072), and N0=320/400 inits with top-15 upscale gave 0.856207 (p0076) — tiny stage 0.852331, upscale +0.0017, restarts +0.0022. The basin landscape is rich and unsaturated.

why: Confirms scaling direction.
statement: The tiny-N global search is far from saturated: going from N0=250/250 inits to N0=320/400 inits gained +0.0038 (p0076). Both the tiny stage and the upscale+restart stages contributed substantially.

why: Largest single-stage restart gain observed.
statement: A dedicated long noisy-restart + block-ascent polish of a good basin (p0072) gains a lot: +0.00313 to 0.855549 (p0079), with the restart stage alone contributing +0.00287. Restart polish is not saturated.

why: Mutation-loop evidence that coordinate polish composes with restarts.
statement: Cheap single-coordinate polish followed by alternating refine/noisy-restart with downscale-relocate gains +0.00238 on p0072 (p0077, mutation loop), confirming coordinate polish is a cheap high-value stage.

why: Continued large gains refute any ceiling claim.

Older low-N basin result; current p0081/p0083 line subsumes it.

statement: Direct peak-dip (multiplicative Gaussian dents near the f*f argmax plus rescale, then block re-ascent) is a real but small lever: p0096 gained +0.000239 on p0089, while in p0095 the dip stage gave only +0.000006 (no real change). It is secondary to upscale/restarts.

why: Three independent runs show the tiny-N stage flat and the upscale stage carrying the gain.
statement: The seeded tiny-N global search's value comes almost entirely from its upscale chain, not the tiny-N basin search: p0091 tiny-N gave ~0 while upscale gave +0.000657; p0097 tiny-N gave 0 while upscale gave +0.00062; p0095 tiny-N gave 0 while upscale gave +0.00098. The tiny-N basin search is saturated.

why: The best score is at the lowest N tried, consistent with saturation above N~1600.
statement: High-N is saturated and may even hurt: N=4000-8000 gains only +0.000229 (p0088), N=2200 gains +0.000029 (p0093), and the best result now sits at N=800 (p0095, 0.860002). Keep effort at N<=1600 and prefer landing near N=800.

why: p0093's 7s coord polish produced zero improvement on the current best basin.
statement: Cheap per-coordinate hill-climb is a strong stage in some basins (p0077 +0.00238, p0085 +0.00157, p0081 +0.0008) but gave exactly 0 on p0091 in p0093, so it is basin-dependent and must not be relied on as the main lever.

why: Gains from restarts have shrunk by an order of magnitude on the newest basin.
statement: Noisy-restart + block-ascent polish still pays but is now small on the current basin: p0095's restart stage gave +0.00020 and polish +0.00015, versus the +0.003 it gave on p0072. Restart polish is a finishing lever, not the main one.

why: Another former plateau (0.8587) was broken by a recipe change.
statement: Every 'plateau' so far (0.8410, 0.8426, 0.8432, 0.8524, 0.8562, 0.8587) has been a recipe artifact: upscale-to-N=800 + peak-dip + restarts has now reached 0.860002 (p0095).

why: p0101's stage lines again show tiny-N flat and upscale/restarts carrying the entire gain.
statement: The seeded tiny-N global search's value comes almost entirely from its upscale chain and noisy restarts, not the tiny-N basin search: p0101 tiny-N gave 0.000000 while upscale gave +0.000551 and restarts gave +0.000400.

why: p0100 confirms peak-dip can pay on a different basin, but below the predicted >=0.0005.
statement: Direct peak-dip is a real but small lever: p0096 gained +0.000239, p0100 gained +0.000279, while p0095's dip stage gave only +0.000006. It is worth combining with upscale/restarts but is secondary to them.

why: p0101 extends the trend that lower final N is better for this line.
statement: Final resolution matters: the best result now sits at N=600 (p0101 0.860953), better than N=800 (p0095 0.860002), N=1600 (p0097 0.859398) and N=2200 (p0093 0.858700). Coarse-to-fine ending near N=600-800 is best.

why: p0101 is another data point that low final N plus upscale beats high-N polishing.
statement: High-N is saturated and may hurt: N=4000-8000 gains only +0.000229, N=2200 gains +0.000029, and the best now sits at N=600 (p0101, 0.860953). Keep effort at N<=1600 and prefer landing near N=600-800.
refuted_if: A high-N (>=4000) refinement of the current best consistently gains more than +0.0005 over the N=600 result.

why: p0101 broke the 0.8600 level with another recipe/schedule change.
statement: Every 'plateau' so far (0.8410, 0.8426, 0.8432, 0.8524, 0.8562, 0.8587, 0.8600) has been a recipe artifact: upscale-to-N=600-800 + peak-dip + restarts has now reached 0.860953 (p0101).
refuted_if: The low-N restart/upscale recipe stalls across multiple independent basins/seeds and no schedule variation gains.

why: p0103 directly tested a 3-6 bump parametric family and landed far below the height-vector line.
statement: The low-dimensional bump-mixture family is not competitive: its best global optimization reached only 0.836444, below 0.85, so height-vector search remains the only competitive construction region found so far.
